claims.text: The starting materials are multi-element, near-equiatomic solid-solution HEA nanoparticles.
Laser solid-phase synthesis on laser-induced graphene supports produces CrMnFeCoNi nanoparticles encapsulated by several graphene layers.
Graphene-shell encapsulation governs preservation of HEA nanoparticle structural and chemical integrity under high-temperature oxidative conditions.
The graphene shell acts as a physical barrier against oxidation.
Oxidation-induced surface changes in equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn correlate with element-specific environmental interactions governed by thermodynamics.
The initial stages of CoCrFeNiMn oxidation are influenced by atomic size and redox potential.
Redox potential becomes the dominant influence as oxidation proceeds.
Oxidation governed by constituent-element redox properties can cause composition inversion.
The graphene shell inhibits oxygen access to the HEA nanoparticle.
Inhibiting oxygen access prevents preferential oxidation and composition inversion in the encapsulated nanoparticles.
Removing or omitting the graphene shell allows the intrinsic oxidation mechanism to proceed unchecked.
Graphene-encapsulated nanoparticles will retain their near-equiatomic composition under the specified oxidative treatment.
Graphene-encapsulated nanoparticles will retain structural integrity under the specified oxidative treatment.
Nanoparticles without graphene shells will exhibit more rapid surface oxidation and composition inversion than encapsulated nanoparticles.
Oxidation and composition inversion in unencapsulated nanoparticles will degrade catalytic or thermoelectric performance.
Graphene encapsulation will provide significant protection over 773–1173 K and potentially up to 1923 K in oxidative atmospheres.
The stability difference between encapsulated and unencapsulated particles may be negligible at substantially lower temperatures or in inert atmospheres.
Atomic size and redox potential may make different relative contributions to oxidation in unencapsulated nanoparticles.
Substrate effects or other synthesis-related variables may influence oxidation behavior.
